extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies' human resources officials, agency counsel, OPM staff, labor unions, and stakeholders affected by adverse-action and excepted-service rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for defining which positions are excepted from chapter 75 protections and the procedures agencies must follow when moving positions between the competitive and excepted services (or among excepted-service schedules), including notice, retention of accrued rights, and appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating' applies to noncareer political appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM defines the phrase as descriptors for positions held by noncareer political employees—positions identified by a close working relationship with the President, head of an agency, or other key appointed officials responsible for furthering the goals and policies of the President and the administration, and that carry no expectation of continued employment beyond the presidential administration during which the appointment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is adopted to reinforce the longstanding interpretation that the exception in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2) applies to political appointees (traditionally Schedule C). OPM is conforming regulatory language across multiple CFR parts (e.g., 210.102, 213.3301, 302.101, 432.101, 451.302, 752.201, 752.401) to standardize phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key distinction: expectation of continuing employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress's 'key to the distinction' between those entitled to appeal/adverse-action rights and those not is the expectation of continuing employment with the Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions/individuals who have an expectation of continued employment beyond the appointing administration generally should retain civil service protections; applying the confidential/policy-making exception to career employees with such expectation would be inconsistent with the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/interpretive standard: longstanding usage since at least 1936
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase and the resulting exception in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2) have historically been understood to mean political appointees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM relied on legislative history, past practice, case law, and decades of MSPB and agency interpretations in adopting the definition. Absent persuasive countervailing evidence, OPM considers the long record dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who determines that a position is 'confidential/policy-determining/etc.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Subparagraphs of 5 U.S.C. 7511(b) assign responsibility for determinations: the President for positions the President has excepted from the competitive service; OPM for positions OPM has excepted; and the President or agency head for positions Congress has excepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations are made by the authority specified in statute (President, OPM, or Congress/agency head) rather than by MSPB or other adjudicatory bodies; agencies must follow delegated standards and procedures when exercising that authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of accrued adverse-action rights when moved involuntarily
rubrics_metrics.description: Incumbents who are involuntarily moved to Schedule C or another excepted-service position retain previously accrued adverse-action rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM clarifies that even where a position is moved into an excepted schedule, an involuntary move does not strip accrued protections; rule text and conforming edits (e.g., to 432.102 and 752 provisions) address this preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SES is governed separately; the phrase does not apply to SES career employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senior Executive Service (SES) is a separate 'service' with its own statutory framework; the confidential/policy-determining/policy-making/policy-advocating phrase as used in 7511(b)(2) does not apply to the SES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career SES employees who have completed the relevant probationary period are covered by SES adverse-action procedures (5 U.S.C. 7541-7543) and retain protections even though SES duties include important policy-making or policy-determining functions. OPM also notes statutory limits on noncareer SES appointments (numerical caps) as additional protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: agencies must follow specific procedures when moving positions between services or schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM revises 5 CFR part 302 to require agencies to follow specified procedures before moving positions from the competitive service to the excepted service (or between excepted-service schedules) following a Presidential, Congressional, OPM, or designee directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures cover OPM oversight, notice requirements for incumbents, and provide a right of appeal to MSPB to the extent a move is involuntary and characterized as stripping previously accrued civil service status and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for departing the competitive service: 'conditions of good administration' / practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Departures from the competitive service must be compelled by 'conditions of good administration' and the authority to except positions is meant to be applied where competitive examination is not practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM historically permits exceptions (e.g., Schedule A for attorneys due to appropriations bar or Schedule D/Pathways programs) where examinations are impracticable or urgent needs exist; OPM will review agency use against the 'conditions of good administration' standard to guard against unsound management practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage exclusions in parts 432 and 752 for policy-making positions (with involuntary-move carve-out)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules clarify that employees in positions determined to be of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character are excluded from coverage under part 432 and part 752 (performance-based and adverse-action rules), consistent with congressional intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM will amend section 432.102(f)(10) (and conform part 752) to add the exception 'unless the incumbent was moved involuntarily to such a position after accruing rights as delineated in paragraph (e) of this section,' thereby preserving rights for incumbents involuntarily moved after accruing protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM will not publish an enumerative list of non-confidential positions
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM declines to provide an enumerated list of positions that do not meet the definition, because it would be impracticable and a partial list might be misunderstood as exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters asked for lists for critical areas (national security, public health, whistleblower protection, audits, legal/regulatory interpretation, budget, research, data analysis), but OPM determined enumeration could generate confusion as new positions are created over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive weight of MSPB and consistent agency interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: MSPB decisions that construe the phrase as shorthand for 'political appointees' are considered persuasive and consistent with OPM's and other agencies' historical interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM considered MSPB case law and congressional reliance on those decisions; while MSPB cannot bind courts, harmonious statutory interpretation reduces agency liability and supports OPM's adopted definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate statutory uses: different language/structure in other statutes (e.g., SES provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Language in other statutory contexts (such as 5 U.S.C. 3132 describing SES duties) uses different formulations and a different statutory structure and therefore should not be read to change the meaning of 7511(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM explains that SES statutory language was written on a clean slate and creates distinct hiring and protection mechanisms; analogies to SES language do not imply that career civil servants outside SES lose adverse-action rights when working on policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and exercise of excepting authority (President and OPM practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may except positions from the competitive service (often via executive orders) and has delegated concurrent authority to OPM to except positions when conditions warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM historically establishes standards/conditions for agencies to apply (e.g., Pathways, Schedule E); some excepted-service uses are prescriptive (specified schedules), others require agencies to apply OPM standards. OPM oversight ensures appropriate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended function of excepted schedules/hiring authorities (pre-determined vs. ad hoc use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some excepted-service schedules are intended as hiring authorities applied prospectively (positions excepted before being filled), while other exceptions may be directive-driven or used to address urgent needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Schedule A attorneys (longstanding exception due to appropriations bar), Schedule D for students/recent graduates, Schedule E (created by Executive Order 13843) intended as a hiring authority; practices differ when incumbents are already in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and informed acceptance for voluntary moves
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM emphasizes that employees who are said to have voluntarily accepted positions that affect their rights should share the same understanding as their agencies and be aware of the potential consequences of those moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring clear notice and understanding helps guard against improper stripping of accrued rights and supports OPM's objective of protecting against prohibited personnel practices and unsound management.
